title: Add rate limiting to public API
summary: Adds per-key token bucket middleware and wires it into the /api routes; /health stays unlimited. Tests cover the allow and reject paths and pass; not load-tested. Verify: the 60/min quota matches the public API docs.

steps.title: Token bucket middleware
steps.description:
This change has three parts: the limiter, its wiring into the router, and tests. We start with the limiter, where each request is counted.

**What:** One token bucket per API key, falling back to client IP; an empty bucket answers `429`.

**Why:** A token bucket allows short bursts up to `capacity` while holding the average rate. A fixed window was simpler, but lets a client double its rate across a window edge.

**Watch for:** `Retry-After` is a constant `1`, not computed from the refill rate.

steps.title: Lazy refill
steps.description:
**What:** The bucket from the previous step is refilled lazily, on each request, from the time since the last one. Nothing runs between requests.

**Why:** No timer means nothing to clean up on shutdown and nothing to leak in tests.

steps.title: Unbounded in-memory state
steps.description:
**What:** Buckets live in a process-local `Map` keyed by API key or IP.

**Watch for:** Nothing ever removes an entry, so a client rotating IPs grows memory without bound. Limits are also per process: behind a load balancer with three instances, a client gets three times the quota. Neither is tested.

steps.title: Scope: `/api` only
steps.description:
**What:** The limiter from the first step is mounted on `/api` only; `/health` stays unlimited.

**Why:** Load balancer probes hit `/health` every few seconds and must never get a `429`. Mounting it app-wide and exempting `/health` inside the limiter was the alternative; it puts routing knowledge into the middleware.

steps.title: Rejection test
steps.description:
**What:** Drains a capacity-1 bucket and checks that the second request gets `429`.

**Watch for:** Refill is switched off (`refillPerSecond: 0`) so the test doesn't depend on wall-clock time, which means the refill path from the second step is not tested at all.
